title: Why Small Goals Boost Your Brain's Motivation
hook: Why does finishing a small task feel so good?

narration.text: Achieving even tiny goals releases dopamine in your brain.
This chemical is crucial for motivation and reward pathways.
Each small success gives a little dopamine hit, reinforcing the behaviour.
Your brain learns to associate effort with a feeling of accomplishment.
This creates a positive feedback loop, increasing your drive.
Breaking down big tasks makes them less daunting and more achievable.
You gain momentum with each small step completed.
This strategy can transform how you approach any challenge.
How do you break down your biggest goals?

description: Discover the surprising science behind why setting small, achievable goals can dramatically increase your motivation. We explain the role of dopamine and how your brain's reward pathways respond to incremental success. Learn how to harness this natural brain mechanism to boost your productivity and reach your biggest aspirations.
topic: Why setting small, achievable goals can increase motivation, explaining the role of dopamine and reward pathways.
